summary: tpu-inference's ragged paged attention v3 Pallas kernel (kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py), the default RPA: ragged_paged_attention(queries, keys, values, kv_cache, kv_lens, page_indices, cu_q_lens, distribution) over a paged KV cache shaped [total_num_pages, page_size, num_kv_heads_x2 // kv_packing, kv_packing, head_dim], K and V interleaved per head and packed by dtype (get_kv_cache_shape); decode, prefill and mixed cases each tuned by (bq_sz, bkv_sz, bq_csz, bkv_csz) block sizes, plus vmem_limit_bytes, chunk_prefill_size, sliding_window, soft_cap and q/k/v scales. Its shape checks: page_size must be a multiple of the KV dtype packing (kv_packing = 32 // bits: 2 for bf16, 4 for fp8/int8); bkv_sz and bkv_csz must be whole pages (multiples of page_size), with bkv_sz % bkv_csz == 0 and bq_sz % bq_csz == 0; head_dim % 128 == 0.
note: Was the kernels directory (tree/main/tpu_inference/kernels): a tree page summarised slowly enough to time out at 600 s twice in the gemma-4-31B-it hill-climb on v6e-8, losing the lookup each time. Now the one file most questions about it reach. The id is kept because pages and evals name it. The other kernels (flash_attention, mla, fused_moe, megablox, quantized_matmul, collectives, sparse_core) are siblings of ragged_paged_attention/ under tpu_inference/kernels/; batched_rpa has its own row (tpu-inference-batched-rpa), and which of the two a server runs is tpu-inference-attention-dispatch.

note: The libtpu environment that lets several processes share one host, which nothing else in the catalog shows.
